extractions.value: Clinical features (muscle stiffness, myoclonus, startle reaction, falls, pontine syndrome), electrophysiological studies (continuous motor unit activity), serum and CSF glycine receptor antibodies, CSF oligoclonal IgG bands, and response to treatment (plasmapheresis, steroids, clonazepam).
extractions.quote: On neurological examination, a severe startle reaction could be triggered by unexpected noises and there was stiffness, especially of the back and lower limb muscles, with myoclonus, lower limb paraparesis, muscle rigidity and increased tendon reflexes without further pyramidal signs. Electrophysiological studies revealed ubiquitous early recruitment and continuous motor unit activity as described for stiff person syndrome. However, serum glycine receptor (GlyR) antibodies were detected by a cell-based assay. Initial lumbar puncture revealed oligoclonal IgG bands and 45 lymphocytes/ll in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). GlyR antibodies could also be found in the patient's CSF. The neurological symptoms ameliorated after an initial therapy of six plasmaphereses followed by oral corticosteroids.
